summary: B is substantially closer to the frozen contract and is the patch I would rather review and merge, although it still needs to delegate Upload to Add and strengthen its tests.
reasons: B adds the exact requested Upload signature and uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field name "file", producing the established buffered, replayable body.
B preserves Add and avoids unrelated retry-transport changes, new options, and API expansion.
B propagates multipart helper errors, validates filename/content before a request, and retains existing FilesOption query and request-option handling.

A explicitly violates scope constraints by adding WithFilesFormFields and NewFileWithFields, association-field behavior forbidden by the contract, and by refactoring generic request-body replay machinery and changing reader-closing semantics.
risks_a: Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request, decoding, and error logic.
The new association-fields API and multipart helper are expressly outside the frozen contract.

The RawClient seek-replay change alters broad SDK behavior and body ownership semantics; its GetBody closures also share one mutable seeker, which is fragile under concurrent or overlapping use versus returning independent readers/reopenings where possible or simply buffering in Upload as required by the contract). It also has questionable handling if seeking to end fails, since GetBody is still installed based on an assumed restorable current offset, and changing whether transport closes caller bodies is an API semantics change unrelated to this task). (typo)
risks_b: Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's implementation and violating an explicit contract requirement.
The Upload test checks the filename but never reads or asserts the uploaded content.

There are no Upload-level tests for retrying streamed source content, validation without a request, or propagation of source-reader failures; the added retry test only covers an already-buffered bytes.Reader and does not inspect replayed body contents.
